newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE meets in bid for deal on Albania force.
newsitem.headline: OSCE meets in bid for deal on Albania force.

text.p: Ambassadors to the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) gathered for an extraordinary meeting on Thursday to try to reach agreement on a foreign security force for Albania.
The permanent council of the 54-member OSCE began convening at 5.35 p.m. (1635 GMT), officials said. A news conference was planned for 6.15 p.m. (1715 GMT).
"They are hopeful of reaching an agreement today," a diplomatic source said.

Talks on Wednesday brought a broad agreement on a humanitarian OSCE mission to strife-torn Albania but failed to yield a consensus on an international force to ensure the safe passage of aid convoys and protect civilian operations.

The permanent council chairman, Danish diplomat Lars Vissing, said some nations were concerned at the lack of a precedent and wanted a United Nations mandate before they backed military assistance. Countries including Italy, Greece, France, Spain and Portugal have said they are ready to send troops.

In Tirana, Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino met a European delegation headed by Dutch diplomat Jan de Marchant et d'Ansembourg on Thursday and repeated his call for foreign help to protect relief supplies, Tirana airport and the main ports.
D'Ansembourg's team includes experts from OSCE, the European Union and its executive Commission and the Council of Europe, which safeguards human rights.
